description: Attach a piece of evidence to an existing lesson and (re)compute its verification status, raising Amplifier's confidence in what it 'knows'. Each call appends one evidence link to the lesson's evidence chain, then promotes status by these rules: any evidence → 'evidence' (confidence 0.7); a 'user_confirmation' evidence OR ≥2 distinct evidence types → 'confirmed' (confidence 1.0); pass promote_to to override the auto-rule. Returns the lesson id, its new status and confidence, the total number of accumulated evidence links, and the latest evidence just added; returns an error if the lesson id does not exist. Use it when a claim gets backed by reality — tests pass, a commit lands, a doc confirms it, or the user explicitly confirms. The target lesson must already exist (created via amplify_record_claim for unverified claims, or amplify_learn_from_mistake); use amplify_evidence_chain afterward to audit why a lesson reached 'confirmed'.

evidence_link.description: Required. The concrete proof itself — a git SHA, test id/name, doc URL, or short note (e.g. 'a1b2c3d', 'test_verifyLesson_promotes', 'https://docs…', 'Ville confirmed in chat').

evidence_type.description: Required. The kind of proof being attached, one of: 'git_commit', 'test_run', 'user_confirmation', 'external_doc', 'manual_review'. Attaching a 'user_confirmation' (or reaching ≥2 distinct types across all evidence) auto-promotes the lesson to 'confirmed'.

id.description: Required. Id of the existing lesson to verify (positive integer; accepts a numeric string too). Must reference a lesson already created via amplify_record_claim or amplify_learn_from_mistake — a non-existent id returns an error.

promote_to.description: Optional. Force the resulting status to 'evidence' (confidence 0.7) or 'confirmed' (confidence 1.0), bypassing the auto-promotion rules. Omit to let evidence-count/type rules decide.

name: amplify_verify_claim
